subject: Post-demo: streaming SLO pilot configs and GPU comparison
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21 14:12 PDT
Subject: Post-demo: streaming SLO pilot configs and GPU comparison

Hi Priya — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our demo and suggested pilot options so we can get you a concrete scope and quote. Attaching a short SLO matrix (dedicated_slo_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a draft pilot quote.

Summary of what you confirmed today:
- Primary workload: live transcription + structured post-processing (streaming responses to web clients).
- Typical request: ~900–1,200 tokens/session, median 1.0s chunk latency target for streaming segments.
- Expected baseline steady traffic: 60–80 reqs/sec; mornings spike to ~180 reqs/sec for 20–30 minutes.
- Compliance: need SOC2 evidence and IP isolation; pilot will run in a dedicated pool / VPC.

SLOs we discussed (please confirm):
- P95 end-to-end latency (first streamed chunk): <= 200 ms
- Sustained throughput: 80 req/s with bursts to 200 req/s for up to 30 min
- Concurrency headroom: 40–60 active concurrent streams
- Stability: <1% 5xx over a one-week pilot window

Pilot configuration options (high-level):
1) Multi-A10G reserved slab (recommended for cost predictability)
   - 4x A10G nodes in a reserved pool; continuous batching + KV prefix cache; estimated headroom to cover sustained 80 rps and spikes to 200 rps with graceful degradation policy.
   - Pros: lower unit cost, good streaming RTX-style throughput.
   - Cons: more nodes to manage; slightly higher cold-start for very long contexts.

2) Mixed slab with 1x H100 + 2x A10G (performance-first)
   - H100 handles tail-latency-sensitive inference; A10G handles most steady-state requests.
   - Pros: best single-request latency for the heaviest models.
   - Cons: higher cost; less predictable unit economics during bursts.

Next steps we recommend:
- You confirm the SLO numbers above and the preferred pilot start window (we have capacity the week of July 8).
- We provision a 2-week pilot slab (can be 4x A10G or mixed H100/A10G) and run a benchmark against a representative request set (please share your 2000-request sample).
- We provide an MPA for the pilot scope and a short SOC2 snapshot.

Questions for you: what percentage of sessions require real-time token-by-token streaming vs batched/near-real-time? Also confirm whether spikes are bursty (short, 10–30m) vs sustained.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa on the technical bench and Ben on commercial if you want pricing options upfront.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming SLO pilot configs and GPU comparison

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Streaming patterns: ~70% of sessions are true streaming (token-by-token to the web client). The other 30% are near-real-time (we can accept 500–800ms batch response).
- Average transcript length: ~1,000 tokens; peak long sessions up to 8,000 tokens (rare).
- Spikes: morning spikes are bursty and happen for ~25 minutes, often starting with a large fan-in event (push notification).
- Regulatory: we need audit logs for token retention and ability to stovepipe logs to our SIEM.

Pilot asks:
1) Recommend a configuration that keeps first-chunk p95 <= 200ms across steady + spike windows.
2) Show cost delta between the pure A10G slab vs mixed H100 option (we care about both $/req and tail latency).
3) Confirm what telemetry we can send to our SIEM and the retention window for logs during pilot.

We can share the 2k request sample next business day. July 8 window looks good for a start — prefer July 9 if you have an available bench.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform, HealthSync AI
priya@healthsync.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@healthsync.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22 09:11 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo: streaming SLO pilot configs and GPU comparison

Priya — great context. Quick technical readout and a conservative pilot config we can operate during the 2-week test.

On latency and spikes:
- For token-by-token streaming, the main tail factors are kernel efficiency (H100 wins) and KV cache effectiveness (helps avoid repeated prefix compute). We’ll enable prefix KV caching and tune batch windows to prioritize first-chunk latency (short windowing for streaming).

Conservative pilot config (goal: p95 first-chunk <= 200ms across steady+spike):
- Reserved slab: 4x A10G nodes 
  - Runtime: continuous batching with streaming-optimized kernel path
  - Autoscale buffer: 30% burst capacity (policy-based); when bursting > sustained, requests are routed to pre-warmed async lane on a warm A10G node to avoid head-of-line blocking.
  - KV cache: pre-warm common prefixes for customer’s top-100 prompts
  - Expected headroom: sustained 80 rps + spikes to 180 rps (tested with our internal benchmark using 1k-token median sample)

Optional faster-tail configuration (if HealthSync requires tighter tail latency)
- Mixed slab: 1x H100 + 2x A10G (H100 handles the heaviest contexts and any long-session tails)
  - Expected improvement: ~20–35% p95 reduction on heavy contexts; cost delta ~+40–60% vs 4x A10G depending on commit term.

Telemetry and logs:
- We can stream per-request traces and token-level latency metrics to your SIEM via our secure ingestion endpoint (TLS + signed webhook). Pilot retention: 30 days by default; can extend for pilot at no extra charge to 90 days. Audit artifacts: model version, route, and request hashes available for SOC2 review.

Bench plan / acceptance criteria:
- Day 0–2: provision slab and run synthetic benchmark with your 2k sample.
- Day 3–9: shadow traffic run from a subset of prod (non-PII) to validate latency and error rate.
- Day 10–14: live pilot with full routing and monitoring; we validate SLOs and produce a runbook for full deployment.

Commercial note (Ben): we’ll supply two quote lines for the pilot (4x A10G reserved 2-week vs mixed H100/A10G) and an extrapolated monthly commit for production.

If you confirm the 4x A10G pilot, we’ll provision for July 9 and start the synthetic benchmark the same day.

—Marissa
